# Movie Words

> What ~51,000 films actually say. Movie Words reduces the English subtitles of 51,624 films to word frequencies and compares them with log-odds to surface each film's, decade's, and genre's signature vocabulary. Only derived word counts are published - no subtitle text is redistributed.

Movie Words is a static, serverless site: the UI reads pre-baked JSON and runs SQL in the browser (DuckDB-WASM) over data on a public Cloudflare R2 bucket at https://data.moviewords.org. Non-English films are counted from their English subtitles (translations), which is clearly labelled in the UI.

## Explore
- [Home](https://moviewords.org): search any film and browse its signature words
- [Trends](https://moviewords.org/#/trends): how words rise and fall across the decades
- [Facts](https://moviewords.org/#/leaderboard): records, superlatives and trivia
- [Compare](https://moviewords.org/#/compare): films, decades or genres head-to-head
- [Decades](https://moviewords.org/#/decades): vocabulary by decade
- [Genres](https://moviewords.org/#/genres): vocabulary by genre

## Data
- [Films index (JSON)](https://data.moviewords.org/all/json/movies-index.json): 51,624 films with title, year, genres, runtime, rating and total word count
- [Languages manifest (JSON)](https://data.moviewords.org/all/json/languages.json): selectable original languages and their film counts
- [Word frequencies by year (Parquet)](https://data.moviewords.org/all/word_year.parquet): per-word counts per year across the whole corpus
- [Year totals (JSON)](https://data.moviewords.org/all/json/year-totals.json): total words per year (rate denominators)
- Per-film word counts (JSON): https://data.moviewords.org/all/json/movie/IMDB_ID.json (e.g. https://data.moviewords.org/all/json/movie/tt0068646.json)

## Documentation
- [README](https://github.com/beveradb/moviewords/blob/main/README.md): project overview

## Notes
- Subtitles are not scripts, and the corpus is partial (it skews modern and popular films).
- Non-English films are measured from their English subtitles, not their original-language dialogue.
- Dialogue is from the OPUS OpenSubtitles corpus; film metadata from IMDb and TMDB. See the FAQ for attribution and licensing.
